paragraphs.title: David’s Old Age and Adonijah’s Rise

answers: He was old and could not get warm
easy.explanation: David was old and stricken in years, and he could not get warm.
easy.q: What was David’s condition at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: Abishag was brought to cherish and minister unto David.
easy.q: Who was brought to serve David?

easy.explanation: Adonijah exalted himself and said, “I will be king.”

answers: To cherish and minister unto him
medium.explanation: David’s servants sought a young woman to cherish him and help him get heat.
medium.q: Why was Abishag brought to David?

answers: He raised himself up and claimed greatness
medium.explanation: Adonijah promoted himself by claiming that he would be king.
medium.q: What does “exalted himself” mean in this passage?

answers: He prepared chariots, horsemen, and fifty runners
medium.explanation: Adonijah prepared royal symbols and attendants for himself.
medium.q: What did Adonijah do to present himself as a ruler?

answers: Adonijah had not been disciplined by his father for his conduct
challenge.explanation: David had not displeased Adonijah or asked him why he acted as he did.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from David’s failure to correct Adonijah previously?

challenge.explanation: Joab and Abiathar helped Adonijah, but Zadok was not with him.
challenge.q: Which person did not join Adonijah?

answers: He acted as though he were taking the kingdom for himself
challenge.explanation: Excluding Solomon and his supporters showed Adonijah’s attempt to seize the throne.
challenge.q: What does Adonijah’s failure to invite Solomon and his supporters show?

paragraphs.title: Nathan and Bathsheba Act to Save Solomon

easy.explanation: Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother.
easy.q: To whom did Nathan speak about Adonijah’s actions?

easy.explanation: Nathan warned Bathsheba to save her own life and Solomon’s life.
easy.q: Whom did Nathan tell Bathsheba to save?

easy.explanation: Bathsheba went in unto King David.
easy.q: To whom did Bathsheba go to speak?

answers: His oath that Solomon would reign after him
medium.explanation: Nathan told her to remind David of his oath concerning Solomon.
medium.q: What did Nathan tell Bathsheba to remind David of?

medium.explanation: Nathan warned Bathsheba to protect herself and Solomon from danger.
medium.q: What does “save thine own life” mean in this context?

answers: Adonijah was reigning without David’s knowledge
medium.explanation: She said, “Adonijah reigneth; and now, my lord the king, thou knowest it not.”
medium.q: What fact did Bathsheba emphasize to David?

answers: To confirm and support her words
challenge.explanation: Nathan said that he would come in after her and confirm her words.
challenge.q: Why did Nathan plan to enter David’s chamber after Bathsheba?

answers: Adonijah held a feast and invited supporters, but Solomon and his supporters were excluded
Solomon held a feast while Adonijah was excluded
challenge.explanation: They emphasized Adonijah’s feast and the exclusion of Solomon and his supporters.
challenge.q: What contrast did Bathsheba and Nathan present to David?

answers: To persuade David to fulfill his promise to Solomon immediately
To ask David to appoint Adonijah
challenge.explanation: They sought David’s clear action concerning who would sit on his throne.
challenge.q: What was the purpose of Bathsheba and Nathan’s appeals?

easy.explanation: David called Bathsheba to come before him.
easy.q: Whom did David call after hearing Bathsheba and Nathan?

answers: Make Solomon king that same day
easy.explanation: David swore that Solomon would reign after him that day.
easy.q: What did David swear to do?

easy.explanation: David commanded that Solomon be brought down to Gihon.
easy.q: Where did David command Solomon to be brought?

medium.explanation: David summoned Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah and gave them the command.
medium.q: Who was commanded to carry out Solomon’s coronation?

medium.explanation: David used the phrase as a solemn oath.
medium.q: What does “As the Lord liveth” indicate in David’s speech?

answers: The trumpet would sound and the people would proclaim Solomon king
Solomon would return to his chamber
Adonijah would be invited to reign
medium.explanation: David commanded them to blow the trumpet and say, “God save king Solomon.”
medium.q: What was to happen after Solomon was anointed?

answers: Solomon would be David’s successor and king
Solomon would only serve the king
Solomon would be sent to Gihon without authority
challenge.explanation: Sitting on David’s throne represented succession to the kingdom.
challenge.q: What did seating Solomon on David’s throne signify?

challenge.explanation: David appointed Solomon to be ruler over Israel and over Judah.
challenge.q: What additional position did David give Solomon besides being king?

answers: He asked to delay the ceremony
He said “Amen” and prayed that the Lord would be with Solomon
challenge.explanation: Benaiah accepted the command and asked that the Lord be with Solomon.
challenge.q: How did Benaiah respond to David’s command?

easy.explanation: Solomon rode upon King David’s mule.
Zadok took a horn of oil and anointed Solomon.
The people said, “God save king Solomon,” and rejoiced with great joy.
easy.q: How did the people respond to Solomon’s coronation?

answers: Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and the royal guard
medium.explanation: Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went with him.

answers: The tremendous volume of the people’s rejoicing
medium.explanation: The expression emphasizes the great volume of the joyful sound.
medium.q: What does “the earth rent with the sound of them” describe?

answers: The people made a great noise nearby
David sent messengers to silence them
medium.explanation: The city rang with the sound of the celebration.
medium.q: Why did the trumpet and rejoicing reach Adonijah’s feast?

answers: Adonijah feasted with his supporters, while Solomon was crowned by David’s command with the people’s rejoicing
challenge.explanation: Solomon’s coronation followed David’s official command and involved public celebration.
challenge.q: What was the main difference between Adonijah’s feast and Solomon’s coronation?

answers: Anointing, riding, and then David’s command
Riding to Gihon, anointing, trumpet blowing, and the people’s rejoicing
challenge.explanation: Solomon was taken to Gihon, anointed, publicly proclaimed, and celebrated.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes Solomon’s coronation?

challenge.explanation: The royal mule and anointing oil were signs of Solomon’s official kingship.
challenge.q: What did the mule and the horn of oil symbolize?

easy.explanation: The passage says that Solomon sat on the throne of the kingdom.
easy.q: Who sat on the throne of the kingdom?

easy.explanation: The king’s servants came to bless David and his son.
easy.q: What did David’s servants do after Solomon was crowned?

easy.explanation: Adonijah’s guests were afraid and went every man his way.
easy.q: What did Adonijah’s guests do when they heard about Solomon?

answers: They heard that Solomon had been made king with David’s approval
medium.explanation: They realized that Solomon’s coronation had David’s authority.
They feared the consequences when they learned that Solomon was king.
medium.q: What does “were afraid” indicate about Adonijah’s guests?

answers: The blessing showed acceptance of Solomon, causing Adonijah’s supporters to fear
The blessing was meant to restore Adonijah
medium.explanation: The blessing and report made clear who had been accepted as king.
medium.q: What connection exists between David’s servants blessing Solomon and Adonijah’s guests fleeing?

answers: It depended on political support rather than David’s approval
He was already the universally accepted king
challenge.explanation: When David’s approval of Solomon became known, Adonijah’s support collapsed.
challenge.q: What does the reaction of Adonijah’s guests reveal about his position?

answers: David’s servants blessed, while Adonijah’s guests feared and dispersed
challenge.explanation: David’s servants welcomed the succession, while Adonijah’s guests panicked.
challenge.q: What difference appears between David’s servants and Adonijah’s guests?

challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the gathering dissolved and no longer acted as one group.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the phrase “went every man his way”?

easy.explanation: Adonijah caught hold on the horns of the altar.
Solomon told Adonijah, “Go to thine house.”
easy.q: What did Solomon say to Adonijah at the end of the passage?

answers: That he would not slay him with the sword
That he would make him a priest
That he would give him the kingdom
medium.explanation: Adonijah asked Solomon not to kill his servant with the sword.
medium.q: What did Adonijah ask Solomon to swear?

answers: A man who conducts himself properly and loyally
A man with physical strength only
A man who flees the city
medium.explanation: Solomon made Adonijah’s safety dependent on honorable conduct.
medium.q: What does “a worthy man” mean in Solomon’s statement?

answers: If he proved himself worthy and did not act wickedly
If he became king instead of Solomon
If he invited all Israel to a feast
medium.explanation: Solomon warned that wickedness found in Adonijah would result in death.
medium.q: On what condition did Solomon allow Adonijah to live?

answers: He was preparing to offer a sacrifice
challenge.explanation: Adonijah feared for his life and sought sanctuary at the altar.
challenge.q: What does Adonijah’s grasping the altar’s horns show about his condition?

answers: He released Adonijah but warned him not to act wickedly
challenge.explanation: Solomon allowed Adonijah to go home while setting a serious condition for his safety.
challenge.q: How did Solomon combine mercy with caution?

answers: At first he presented himself as king, but later he feared and sought protection
At first he was a prisoner, but later he became king
At first he supported Solomon, but later he crowned David
challenge.explanation: Adonijah changed from a self-appointed claimant to a frightened man seeking mercy.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in Adonijah’s position at the beginning and end of the chapter?
